mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined in each of the last four weekly means (-26.3 to -27.9), indicating a self-reinforcing contraction trend driven by continued consumer caution; this momentum is predicted to persist, producing a further decline in RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically across all four weeks (-26.3,-27.1,-27.7,-27.9)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is higher than its 28-day trailing mean despite the four-week monotonic decline, indicating the momentum effect reversed.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in WORKPLACES from -31.0 to -17.1/-17.6 over the last two weeks signals loosening of work-from-home policies or reopening of offices; once WORKPLACES crosses above -15, induced commuting and lunchtime/after-work shopping trips are expected to lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -15 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat for two weeks after WORKPLACES crosses -15, despite the proposed commuting-driven retail boost.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has remained flat near -25 to -27 while WORKPLACES rebounded sharply, suggesting workers are shifting to private vehicles rather than public transit for commuting. This modal shift reduces foot traffic near transit-adjacent retail corridors, sustaining RETAIL_REC's decline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed between -25.3 and -27.1 while WORKPLACES rose 13+ points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks even though TRANSIT remains flat and WORKPLACES keeps rising, indicating no modal-shift penalty on retail.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility fell sharply from -13.7 to -28.1 over the last two weeks, consistent with mid-January cold-weather reduction in outdoor activity. Because retail options are simultaneously constrained by pandemic restrictions, there is no indoor substitution, so RETAIL_REC is expected to continue declining over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks despite continued PARKS decline, indicating seasonal outdoor-indoor substitution is occurring.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility rebounded from 22.0 to 25.7 in the last week while RETAIL_REC continued to fall, consistent with a post-holiday tightening of retail restrictions that spares essential grocery/pharmacy trips. In a regime of renewed restrictions, this divergence is expected to persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 22.0 to 25.7 while RETAIL_REC fell from -27.7 to -27.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM both rise together over the next four weeks, indicating restrictions eased rather than tightened.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated near +12 to +15 percent above baseline, reflecting sustained at-home behavior that substitutes for in-person retail visits. This elevated residential baseline is expected to suppress RETAIL_REC over the coming week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 12.1 and 15.0 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week even though RESIDENTIAL stays above +10, indicating no suppression effect from elevated home time.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week rise in GROCERY_PHARM of more than 3 points (as seen from 22.0 to 25.7) signals consumers substituting discretionary retail trips with essential grocery/pharmacy trips. Once this threshold is crossed, RETAIL_REC is predicted to decline further over the following two weeks due to this substitution effect.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 3.7 points from t-1w (22.0) to t-0w (25.7)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks despite the GROCERY_PHARM jump exceeding the 3-point threshold.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of rising WORKPLACES (from -31.0 to -17.6) and falling RESIDENTIAL (from 15.0 to 12.1) indicates a return-to-office pattern that reduces daytime flexibility for retail errands, since workers spend more time commuting and in offices rather than near home retail. This joint shift is predicted to further depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 13.4 points while RESIDENTIAL fell 2.9 points over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks even as WORKPLACES continues rising and RESIDENTIAL continues falling, indicating no return-to-office penalty on retail.
